name: Clofibrate

own_problems.text: Pulled from the market in Israel and 2 other countries, first in 1979 — for blood vessel problems and cancer risk

similar.name: Beclobrate
problems: Pulled from the market in Switzerland, first in 1990 — for liver harm

similar.name: Cloforex
problems: Pulled from the market in Germany and Sweden, first in 1969 — for breathing problems and heart harm

similar.name: Chlorphentermine
problems: Pulled from the market in Germany and Venezuela, first in 1967 — for breathing problems and heart harm

summary: Clofibrate was pulled from the market in Israel and two other countries starting in 1979 due to blood vessel damage (vascular harm) and the potential to cause cancer (carcinogenicity) [3]. Related drugs were also removed from various markets for liver harm, lung or breathing issues (respiratory harm), and heart harm [3]. In addition, a small computer model, rather than tests on people, calculated low risk scores for heart and liver issues [M].
